She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the wrong for not hosting Thanksgiving like I planned to. Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, for about 50 years, my mom has been hosting Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for all her children and grandchildren. That's a long-standing tradition, and it means a lot to everyone involved. Now, my mom is getting too old to keep doing this, so she asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are four of us, and we're rotating who hosts each holiday. So far, each of us has hosted one holiday. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family is spread out all over the country, and we've never really spent Thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with them. We're not as close to them, so it's not something we've done before. However, this year, her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City. At first, it was just a sister's trip, but then they invited all their kids and grandkids to meet up there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because she thinks it's a "once in a lifetime event," and I agree with her. Plus, I want to go too. As soon as we decided to go to New York for the parade, I called my older brother to see what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He told me that our oldest sister is probably going to be really upset and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck, which didn't make me feel any better. So I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably have to end up hosting Thanksgiving even though it's her turn for Christmas, and she's been planning for it all year. She accused me of being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do and said, "Mom wouldn't abandon Thanksgiving to go to NYC." She went on about how sad Mom will be that I'm doing this. I tried to offer solutions. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother mentioned that his wife might be up for hosting, but he didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't do it because she's renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn, but I tried to come up with solutions. I also offered to host the next holiday, but my oldest sister said no because it's her turn and she's been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother, so I suggested that me and him could maybe just swap Thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here? I'm not sure. On one hand, I have a long-standing family tradition that I agreed to take over when my mom couldn't anymore. It's important to keep that going, especially since it's been a part of our family for so many years. On the other hand, this trip to New York with my wife's family seems like a unique opportunity that we all want to take advantage of. It's not something that comes up every year, and it's important for my wife and daughter to connect with their extended family. I also feel like I've tried to make things work by offering to pay for catering or even hosting the next holiday. But my sister is really upset, and she feels like I'm abandoning our mom's tradition. I don't want to make her or our mom sad, but I also don't want to miss out on this special event with my wife and daughter. Maybe I should have communicated better with my sister earlier on. If I had told her sooner that I wanted to go to New York, maybe we could have figured something out together. But I didn't, and now she's upset. I also feel like my brother isn't too happy about the idea of his wife hosting, which adds another layer of complexity. I guess I'm torn between honoring our family tradition and taking advantage of this unique opportunity with my wife's family. Both are important to me, but I'm not sure how to balance them. I don't want to feel like I'm letting my family down, but I also don't want to miss out on something that could be really meaningful for my wife and daughter. Maybe I should talk to my sister again and see if there's a way to compromise. Perhaps we could have a smaller gathering or find another way to keep the tradition alive without me hosting. Or maybe my brother's wife is willing to host after all, and we could make it work somehow. I just don't want to be the one causing conflict in the family, especially around such an important holiday. In the end, I think I need to weigh the importance of the tradition against the importance of this trip. Is it worth potentially damaging family relationships to go to New York, or should I prioritize keeping the tradition alive? I'm not sure, but I do feel like I've tried to be considerate and find solutions, even if it didn't work out perfectly.
